messages:
Alex (CS): Quick follow-up thread — we need a short customer note + status page copy for the embeddings incident yesterday. Goal: clear timeline, what customers saw, mitigation, and what we’re doing next (RCA + credits). Draft below; please push edits. Incident ID: INC-2026-0429

incident_bot: Incident INC-2026-0429 status changed -> resolved. Trigger: alerting-autoscaler. Severity: P2. Notifying oncall.

Maria (Oncall): Timeline from the runbook: 14:03 UTC - spike in 5xxs for embeddings routes; 14:07 - autoscaler compile queue backlog appears; 14:18 - multiple routing circuit-breakers tripped causing fallback to degraded pool; 14:30 - manual routing change to fallback pool; 14:48 - traffic normalized and errors stopped. I collected traces and a couple of heapdumps.

Sam (SRE): Short tech summary: race in autoscaler when concurrent compile backlog + routing updates caused workers to be marked unhealthy erroneously. That opened thrash between routing and worker recycle. Mitigation: manual routing change -> gave immediate relief. Short-term fix: tune circuit-breaker thresholds and hotfix autoscaler check in v1.3.2 (backport PR ready). Long-term: add stronger guard + observability for compile backlog.

Elena (PM): Proposed status page blurb (2 lines): "Resolved: We fixed an issue affecting embeddings generation that caused errors and elevated latencies between 14:03 and 14:48 UTC. Impact: some requests returned errors or experienced longer response times." Link to full post-incident when RCA is ready.

Jordan (Support): Customer email draft suggestion (keep concise):

Hi —

We want to let you know we experienced a partial interruption affecting embeddings requests on <date> from ~14:03–14:48 UTC. Some requests returned errors or saw increased latency. Our on-call team restored service by rerouting traffic and deploying a mitigation; a full RCA is in progress.

We will provide a one-time service credit for customers impacted during the window; your account rep will follow up with specifics if you were affected.

Thanks for your patience,
Redwood Inference Support

Alex (CS): I like that. Two questions: 1) Should we quantify the credit formula in the note or handle privately? 2) Do we include a pointer to the rollback/mitigation steps?

Jordan (Support): Keep the public note generic re credits ("one-time service credit"). For customers with high impact we'll follow up with exact amounts privately. For mitigation, one sentence: "we rerouted traffic to a stable pool and applied a hotfix" is enough.

Sam (SRE): Additions: include a short internal link for customers with config-sensitive setups: `https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0429/affected-apis` (internal-only until we publish). Also: copy of the quick mitigation commands we ran for oncall handoff: 
```
# manual routing change
redwoodctl route set --pool stable-pool --selector embeddings --force
# restart autoscaler worker
kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler -n inference
```

Maria (Oncall): For the post-incident timeline in the RCA, I can attach the error-rate graphs and the autoscaler logs (14:00–15:00 UTC). Action item: Sam to merge hotfix PR and plan rollout, Maria to collect logs and screenshots, Alex to send initial customer note, Jordan to follow up 1:1 on credits.

Elena (PM): Also propose adding a preventative action for product: temporarily increase circuit-breaker thresholds for heavy compile windows until the backport is live. Assign to eng-runtime.

Alex (CS): Final draft for status page + customer email below — please ack or edit.

Status page (short):
"Resolved: An issue impacted embeddings generation between 14:03–14:48 UTC UTC. Some customers experienced request errors or increased latency. Service has been restored and we are publishing a full RCA with mitigation steps and credits shortly."

Customer email (short):
Hi <Customer>,

We experienced a partial interruption affecting embeddings requests on <date> from ~14:03–14:48 UTC. During that time some requests returned errors or experienced elevated latency. Our on-call team restored service by rerouting traffic to a stable pool and applying a hotfix.

We will follow up with a detailed RCA and issue a one-time service credit to impacted customers. If you saw errors or degraded performance, please reply to this message and we’ll prioritize your case.

Thanks,
Alex on behalf of Redwood Inference Support

Maria (Oncall): ACK — timeline + logs ready, adding traces to the RCA doc.

Sam (SRE): ACK — PR queued for merge, will start rollout after 1 hour smoke verification.

Jordan (Support): ACK — will prepare a list of likely impacted accounts for private follow-ups.

Elena (PM): ACK — I'll schedule the post-mortem write-up and publishing cadence for the RCA + status page.

Alex (CS): Great, I'll post the status page and send the customer email in the next 30 minutes. Action items: Sam (merge + rollout), Maria (attach logs), Jordan (impact list), Elena (publish RCA).
